legacy_cards.title: Establish the public facade and explicit typed composition
legacy_cards.body:
## Goal
Provide the smallest framework-neutral AgentKit API and composition root needed to construct and own one runtime from explicit typed objects.

## Context
The red-team review retains a public Agent facade, narrow ports, and a flat immutable RuntimeSpec while rejecting a v1 registry/DAG, named bindings, scope hierarchy, profiles, and independent wheels. This is the minimal-slice foundation; the DeepSeek-Harness-inspired plugin host remains staged.

## Scope
- Define framework-neutral public values and narrow Protocols for Model, Tool, and SessionRepository sufficient for the slice.
- Define an immutable, strictly validated RuntimeSpec for one model, ordered tools, one session repository, and bounded invocation limits.
- Expose create_agent(spec) as an async context manager plus public Agent.invoke/Agent.stream.
- Use explicit constructor/composition-root wiring and one runtime-owned AsyncExitStack.
- Build one agentkit distribution with internal subpackages.

## Out of Scope
- Entry points, plugin manifests, registry/DAG, capability versions, independent wheels, hot reload, LangGraph, provider SDKs, persistence schemas, profiles/Hydra, generic hooks/events, or DI scope hierarchy.

## Architectural Constraints
- Public contracts must not import agent frameworks, provider SDKs, or storage drivers.
- Adapters depend on contracts; contracts never depend on adapters.
- Runtime resources and explicit invocation context are the only lifetimes; session is data.
- Cleanup is best-effort resource cleanup, not deterministic reversibility.
- Planning only: this card does not dispatch work. If separately dispatched, it authorizes only this card on a dedicated task branch; it does not authorize other-card work, backlog expansion, merges, direct changes to main, or autonomous follow-on implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A consumer constructs a valid RuntimeSpec from typed fakes and enters/exits create_agent(spec).
- Invalid limits, duplicate tool names, and unknown loader keys fail before runtime work.
- Public signatures contain no framework types.
- The project builds as one wheel and strict typing covers the public path.
- Acquisition failure unwinds acquired resources in LIFO order.

## Tests
- Focused RuntimeSpec, facade, and acquisition-rollback tests.
- Strict mypy and ruff checks over public modules.
- Build the wheel and inspect its contents.

## Dependencies
- None.

## Deliverables
- Public facade, contracts, spec, composition root, boundary tests, and minimal fake-component documentation.

## Reviewer Focus
Check dependency direction, framework/config leakage, globals/service-locator behavior, premature abstractions, cleanup on failure, and API breadth.

legacy_cards.title: Implement safe bounded model and tool invocation
legacy_cards.body:
## Goal
Deliver one model → tool → model path whose tool execution is forced through a kernel-owned ToolInvoker and whose stream has bounded terminal behavior.

## Context
Tool authorization, validation, audit, timeout, and cancellation are enforcement points, not optional plugins. The slice uses a native loop and closed product events, not a framework event union or speculative loop-port abstraction.

## Scope
- Implement the minimal native model/tool loop.
- Implement a non-bypassable ToolInvoker that validates name/schema, propagates principal/context, obtains allow/deny, audits, enforces timeout, and invokes the tool.
- Define closed events for text delta, tool requested/started/completed/failed, final result, failure, and cancellation.
- Own tasks with structured concurrency and enforce one terminal outcome.
- Enforce iteration, tool-call, payload, and timeout limits.

## Out of Scope
- Generic middleware/hooks, retries/fallback frameworks, real sandbox/approval UI, provider SDKs, LangGraph, durable resume, parallel graphs, or persistence implementation.

## Architectural Constraints
- No tool is reachable from the loop except through ToolInvoker.
- Policy failures deny by default; validation precedes policy/execution.
- Cancellation leaves no orphan task or post-terminal event.
- Public stream/errors are provider and framework neutral.
- Planning only: this card does not dispatch work. If separately dispatched, it authorizes only this card on a dedicated task branch; it does not authorize other-card work, backlog expansion, merges, direct changes to main, or autonomous follow-on implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A fake model/tool completes model → tool → model in specified event order.
- Invalid arguments and denied policy prove the tool body was not called.
- Timeout/cancellation during model and tool work yield exactly one terminal outcome and no orphan tasks.
- Bounds fail closed.
- An architecture test guards the ToolInvoker-only path.

## Tests
- Happy-path event ordering; schema/policy denial; timeout; cancellation; limits; task-leak and post-terminal assertions.

## Dependencies
- AK-001.

## Deliverables
- Native loop, closed stream, ToolInvoker, policy seam, invocation context, tests, and execution invariants.

## Reviewer Focus
Look for bypasses, fail-open policy, cancellation races, task leaks, multiple terminals, unbounded data, sensitive audit content, and framework-shaped semantics.

legacy_cards.title: Persist only product-required session messages and tool audit records
legacy_cards.body:
## Goal
Provide minimal continuity for completed messages and run/tool audit records without claiming event sourcing, execution replay, or framework-independent reconstruction.

## Context
The red-team conclusion governs the slice: model product data directly, keep future adapter checkpoints private, and add sequencing/idempotency only with a demonstrated concurrent-resume need.

## Scope
- Finalize SessionRepository operations used by AK-002 for completed messages, terminal records, and tool audits.
- Implement deterministic, isolated in-memory persistence.
- Add SQLite only if restart continuity is an explicit slice requirement; otherwise document it as gated follow-up.
- Apply redaction and size limits before persistence and use references for large/binary payloads.
- Integrate writes at owned invocation/tool boundaries.

## Out of Scope
- Event sourcing, replay/upcasting/projections, forks, outbox/subscriptions, distributed stores, LangGraph checkpoints, durable HITL, Postgres/KurrentDB, summaries, token deltas, reasoning traces, secrets, or unrestricted tool payloads.

## Architectural Constraints
- Session records are product-shaped; checkpoints are not session truth.
- Contracts are async/framework neutral and adapters depend inward.
- Each visible run has exactly one terminal record consistent with the stream.
- Planning only: this card does not dispatch work. If separately dispatched, it authorizes only this card on a dedicated task branch; it does not authorize other-card work, backlog expansion, merges, direct changes to main, or autonomous follow-on implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Sessions are isolated and deterministically ordered.
- Successful, denied, failed, timed-out, and cancelled tools persist bounded audits.
- Failed/cancelled runs have one terminal record and no false completed assistant message.
- Repository failures do not fake durability.
- Records contain no framework objects, secrets, or oversized artifacts.

## Tests
- Repository contract, ordering/isolation, audit outcomes, terminal consistency, redaction, bounds, serialization, and failure injection.

## Dependencies
- AK-002.

## Deliverables
- Minimal repository contract and memory adapter; optional gated SQLite; integration, tests, and persistence-boundary documentation.

## Reviewer Focus
Check dual-truth/replay overclaims, sensitive payload handling, terminal consistency, concurrency assumptions, framework leakage, and unnecessary fields.

legacy_cards.title: Prove the built wheel in a clean external consumer
legacy_cards.body:
## Goal
Prove the vertical slice from a freshly built artifact: clean install, public import, fake model → tool → model, persistence, cancellation, and cleanup.

## Context
An isolated consumer prevents editable/source-path success from hiding wheel metadata, dependency, import, and lifecycle defects.

## Scope
- Build and non-editably install the wheel in a fresh environment without the repository on PYTHONPATH.
- Create an external consumer using documented APIs and fake components.
- Assert event order, result, persisted message/audit, cancellation, and cleanup.
- Check wheel contents and forbidden public-boundary imports.
- Provide one repeatable command that rebuilds before installing.

## Out of Scope
- PyPI, split wheels, live providers/credentials, network tests, benchmarks, release automation, or implementing defects beyond AK-001–AK-003.

## Architectural Constraints
- Use a newly built non-editable wheel and public imports only.
- Cancellation yields one terminal outcome/no orphan task; each acquired resource closes once.
- Source-tree tests are not substitute evidence.
- Planning only: this card does not dispatch work. If separately dispatched, it authorizes only this card on a dedicated task branch; it does not authorize other-card work, backlog expansion, merges, direct changes to main, or autonomous follow-on implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The isolated consumer imports from its environment and completes the fake path.
- Persistence, denial/failure, cancellation, and cleanup pass.
- Framework/provider packages are unnecessary for the fake path.
- The runner rejects stale/missing builds or private imports.
- Quickstart matches the tested API.

## Tests
- Clean-consumer command; installed-path assertion; wheel metadata/content and forbidden imports; focused suite, lint, and strict typing.

## Dependencies
- AK-001.
- AK-002.
- AK-003.

## Deliverables
- External fixture, isolated runner, wheel proof, boundary assertions, and tested quickstart.

## Reviewer Focus
Check isolation, stale wheels, private imports, undeclared dependencies, cleanup/cancellation, docs drift, and scope broadening.

legacy_cards.title: Spike Python entry-point discovery, imports, and duplicate identity
legacy_cards.body:
## Goal
Time-box a disposable experiment to establish pre-import metadata, load-time execution, and duplicate names/IDs across installed entry-point wheels.

## Context
Entry-point metadata lacks AgentKit manifests, so full graph validation requires importing trusted code. Evidence is required before a public discovery contract. Time box: one working day maximum.

## Scope
- Build two disposable wheels with duplicate entry-point names and agreeing/disagreeing plugin IDs.
- Instrument import and factory-construction side effects; record metadata available before load().
- Test enumeration/selection in fresh environments.
- Compare fail-closed duplicate policies using distribution origin/version, entry-point name, and plugin ID.
- Exit VALIDATED, PARTIAL, or INVALIDATED with evidence and recommendations.

## Out of Scope
- Production discovery/manifests, registry/DAG, runtime version solver, activation lifecycle, independent releases, or retaining spike code as production.

## Architectural Constraints
- Use disposable environments and treat installation as a trusted-code boundary.
- Do not claim load/import is side-effect free or reversible.
- PEP 440 owns install compatibility; no capability-version solver.
- Duplicate recommendations fail closed and name both distributions.
- Planning only: this card does not dispatch work. If separately dispatched, it authorizes only this card on a dedicated task branch; it does not authorize other-card work, backlog expansion, merges, direct changes to main, or autonomous follow-on implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Evidence distinguishes enumerate/select/load/construct/activate.
- Side effects are observed or falsified with markers.
- Duplicate cases have deterministic diagnostics.
- Versions/commands are reproducible.
- Report ends in exactly one required status and lists unknowns.

## Tests
- Rebuild/install fixtures in two fresh environments; capture descriptors before/after load; demonstrate duplicate cases and record versions.

## Dependencies
- None.

## Deliverables
- Time-boxed report, disposable fixtures, raw evidence summary, status, identity/discovery invariants, and adoption gate; no public API.

## Reviewer Focus
Check phase distinctions, isolation, ordering assumptions, import-side-effect honesty, duplicate diagnostics, and avoidance of a second package solver.

legacy_cards.title: Spike LangGraph HITL interrupt and resume translation
legacy_cards.body:
## Goal
Time-box a disposable real LangGraph HITL flow to test translation without leaking graph, checkpoint, interrupt, command, or stream types publicly.

## Context
Simple ReAct parity does not prove replaceability. LangGraph earns inclusion only for durable branching/HITL, while checkpoints remain adapter-private. Time box: two working days maximum.

## Scope
- Build a mutating-tool flow that interrupts, writes a private checkpoint, ends the runtime/process, and resumes approve/deny branches.
- Map minimal product pause/approval/resume events and list lossy concepts.
- Route the fake tool through an AgentKit-style invoker.
- Test graph-revision mismatch and required private metadata.
- Exit VALIDATED, PARTIAL, or INVALIDATED for a private adapter and bounded public promise.

## Out of Scope
- Production adapter/AgentLoopPort, canonical event sourcing, approval UI, deployment/LangSmith, all stream modes, default-loop changes, or claims beyond the tested flow.

## Architectural Constraints
- LangGraph types remain in disposable adapter code.
- Checkpoints are private recovery data, not session truth.
- The mutation executes at most once; approve and deny are proven.
- Cancellation has one terminal outcome and no post-terminal execution.
- Planning only: this card does not dispatch work. If separately dispatched, it authorizes only this card on a dedicated task branch; it does not authorize other-card work, backlog expansion, merges, direct changes to main, or autonomous follow-on implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Approve resume survives runtime/process restart.
- Deny never invokes the tool; repeated resume does not duplicate mutation.
- Graph revision mismatch fails safely.
- No framework type is needed publicly.
- Report ends in one required status with unresolved risks.

## Tests
- Interrupt/restart/approve; deny; duplicate resume; revision incompatibility; cancellation; package-version and stream/checkpoint evidence.

## Dependencies
- None.

## Deliverables
- Time-boxed report, translation table, disposable fixture, evidence, status, proposed boundary/private metadata, and risks; no production API.

## Reviewer Focus
Check restart evidence, idempotency, branch symmetry, revision handling, dual truth, framework leakage, cancellation, and bounded conclusions.

legacy_cards.title: Converge the staged plugin architecture after slice and spike evidence
legacy_cards.body:
## Goal
Record one evidence-based staged architecture that preserves the full DeepSeek-Harness-inspired plugin system as target without retroactively expanding v1.

## Context
The owner chose minimal slice first and full plugin system as staged target. The red-team rejects the old 47-ticket start; assessments identify useful mechanisms. Convergence must use executed evidence.

## Scope
- Review AK-001–AK-004 evidence and both spike reports.
- Create/update an ADR marking ideas retained, deferred, simplified, or killed for v1 and superseding conflicts.
- Define gates for discovery/identity/trust, registry/DAG, lifecycle, config, scopes, hooks/events, wheels, LangGraph HITL, and a future loop contract.
- Map stages to entry criteria, conformance/security tests, and stop conditions.
- Update roadmap decisions and optionally recommend future card boundaries without creating, dispatching, or implementing them.

## Out of Scope
- Production code, plugin/LangGraph implementation, new adapters, package splitting, release work, slice migration, creating/dispatching future cards, merges, main changes, or restoring 47 tickets.

## Architectural Constraints
- The facade and ToolInvoker enforcement remain the base; plugins cannot bypass them.
- Never expose framework types, claim import rollback, add hot unload, or equate checkpoints with session truth.
- New abstractions need two implementations, an external consumer, or measured pain.
- PEP 440 owns package compatibility; runtime identity fails closed.
- Conclusions cite evidence and unknowns.
- Planning only: this card does not dispatch work. If separately dispatched, it authorizes only this card on a dedicated task branch; it does not authorize other-card work, backlog expansion, merges, direct changes to main, or autonomous follow-on implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A decision matrix covers each deferred mechanism and evidence/unknown.
- A dependency diagram has no cycles.
- Every stage has measurable gates, security/conformance tests, and non-goals.
- No implementation authorization beyond these seven cards is introduced.
- Independent review finds no silent contradiction.

## Tests
- Trace every decision to evidence; validate count/DAG; run the architecture security/dependency checklist.

## Dependencies
- AK-004.
- AK-005.
- AK-006.

## Deliverables
- Convergence ADR, evidence matrix, updated gates/non-dispatched recommendations, and reviewer checklist.

## Reviewer Focus
Check evidentiary support, preservation of the minimal slice, translation rather than copying of Cordis ideas, kernel-owned enforcement, and absence of dispatch/implementation/merge/main authorization.
